options.description: Add an explicit target stage to every affected vector and retain exact predicate/stage resolution.
options.existing_vector_effect: Requires decisions for all 18 external-effect vectors and V013; V014 requires selecting the requested later stage.
options.practicality: Good capture shape; producers can bind a target stage if the experiment declares one
options.assessment: Viable amendment shape, but accepted material does not select all required stages.

options.description: Treat external-effect as one stage-less generic predicate and make stage output-only.
options.existing_vector_effect: Could preserve broad outcomes but leaves provider acceptance, occurrence, and recipient acknowledgement boundaries undefined.
options.independent_implementability: FAILS without a new rule for what generic occurrence means
options.partial_effect_compatibility: LOW; PARTIAL_EFFECT has no requested later stage
options.negative_evidence_compatibility: LOW; bounded absence needs a named proposition
options.practicality: Easy to capture but semantically unsafe
options.assessment: Falsified by C's requirement that intended predicate and stage be carried and by the V014 partial-stage case.

options.description: Retain generic external-effect but add an explicit requested minimum/target stage field.
options.existing_vector_effect: Requires a stage for each vector and a rule for minimum-stage satisfaction and partial effect.
options.independent_implementability: HIGH after stage vocabulary and ordering are supplied
options.partial_effect_compatibility: HIGH if the minimum-stage relation is explicit
options.practicality: Capture is plausible but introduces a new target field and comparison semantics
options.assessment: Bounded possibility, not determined by accepted material.

options.description: Use exact stage-specific positive predicates where defined; use a distinct generic-effect contract and a distinct complete-negative contract for the remaining families.
options.existing_vector_effect: Preserves resource-created, recipient acknowledgement, and provider acceptance intent; external-effect and complete-negative need explicit contracts.
options.independent_implementability: HIGH only after the two remaining contracts are written
options.practicality: Best separation of positive and negative capture requirements
options.assessment: Preferred design direction, but not yet a complete normative decision.

falsification_summary.OPTION_B: Rejected as a complete model because it cannot explain V014's earlier-supported/later-unresolved result without a requested target stage.
falsification_summary.OPTION_A: Does not by itself define the missing stage choices; it is a data-shape amendment, not a completed semantic decision.
falsification_summary.OPTION_C: Preserves a generic predicate only by adding new minimum-stage and ordering semantics.
falsification_summary.OPTION_D: Most faithful bounded direction, but still requires a generic-effect contract and a negative proposition contract.
